articleTitle: The development and use of computer applications as a management aid in the power station environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on IT in the Management of Maintenance
abstract: From the start the Maintenance Management at Kilroot Power station (KPS) had defined the role of planning as assisting in providing an effective and economical service of: (1) work control by scheduling and organising the resources; (2) plant condition control by records and analysis; and (3) maintenance costs control by budgetary forecasting and analysis using the technology and resources at hand. To this end, the information processing systems inherited and initiated by the planning function at KPS were adapted and set up to be capable of computer aided interface. The future impact of IT on maintenance work control is also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of computers in maintenance
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on IT in the Management of Maintenance
abstract: The range of equipment maintained by the author's division in briefly outlined. The scale of the fault handling operations and the functions of the repair service control are described. The use of computers in the administration, testing, and progressing of faults is illustrated by describing the LRS100T Line Test System which is used for remote testing of all customer's lines on the public switched network system in British Telecom N. Ireland.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of information technology to asset preservation in Ford of Europe
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on IT in the Management of Maintenance
abstract: The systems described are computer aided maintenance management systems which aid the achievement of the Ford Motor Company's preservation of physical assets policy objectives. The following systems are available for plant and facility management to operate: error diagnostic dynamically indicated methodology; diagnostic overview system; maintenance communication system short term history system; long term combined analysis system; scheduled maintenance system; condition monitoring; online stock control and re-order system; material catalogue; and control of plant engineering contracts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
